channel.title: Marko Lošić — Blog
channel.description: Notes on QA, test automation, mobile and AI testing.

item.title: Manually Testing Chrome and Edge Extensions: Where the Usual Playbook Breaks Down
item.description: Why manual testing of browser extensions needs a different checklist than testing a website, and what to check on Chrome and Edge.

item.title: Risk-Based Testing: How to Decide What Not to Test Before a Deadline
item.description: A practical guide to prioritizing QA coverage by risk when there isn't time to test everything before a release.

item.title: Emulator and Simulator Testing for Mobile Apps: What They Actually Catch, and What They Quietly Miss
item.description: A practical look at testing mobile apps on Android emulators and iOS Simulators, and the common misconceptions that let real bugs through.

item.title: Testing Idempotency: How to Catch Duplicate-Charge Bugs Before Your Users Do
item.description: A practical walkthrough of testing idempotency keys in payment and checkout flows, with concrete test cases for catching duplicate charges.

item.title: Testing the Retry Button: Catching Duplicate-Charge Race Conditions Before Customers Do
item.description: Why sequential idempotency tests miss checkout double-charge bugs, and how to design a test that exposes the real race.

item.title: What the TrueNorth Program Actually Is, and What It Can Do for a Company
item.description: Inside the TrueNorth guide-led training model: what it teaches, how the team guide role works, and the real business case for companies.

item.title: Quality Starts Before the First Line of Code: How I Approach QA
item.description: Why QA that begins at requirements, blends testing types, and closes the loop after release builds real product quality.

item.title: Self-Healing Tests: What They Actually Fix, and What They Quietly Break
item.description: Self-healing test tools patch broken selectors automatically, but they can also hide the very defects your suite exists to catch. Here's how to use them safely.

item.title: Asserting Too Early: The Quiet Source of Flaky Playwright Tests
item.description: Many flaky Playwright tests aren't slow, they check too early. How instant checks and missing awaits cause false failures and false passes.

item.title: Why Maestro Deserves a Spot in Your Web Testing Toolkit
item.description: Maestro is known as a mobile UI testing tool, but its browser support quietly closes the gap with web testing. Here's why I reach for it, and how to write your first flow.
